{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Ch8Lxo3X8jc5hYQyzoDUi","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Coordinate descent paths are now 2.5–20x faster on the target inputs, depending on the kind of input. In my comparisons against a saved copy of the original module, results matched on every case: all 240 randomized cases across the six categories were within the 1e-6 bound with equal `n_iters`, and none of 290 CV fits picked a different `alpha_`. The tests under `sklearn/linear_model/tests`, plus the covariance, dict-learning, feature-selection and common estimator tests that use these solvers, all pass.\n\n## Why it was slow\nEvery alpha along the path recomputed setup work that is about the cost of a full pass over `X`:\n- the column norms;\n- the residuals `R = y - X @ w`;\n- `X.T @ R` for the first convergence check;\n- `Q @ w` in the Gram solver.\n\nOften this setup cost more than the coordinate updates themselves. For sparse `X` with an intercept it is worse: the centering loops run over every sample for every feature, even where the coefficient is zero.\n\n## Change\n- **Solvers (`_cd_fast.pyx`)**: each of the four solvers takes optional arguments for that state (`norm2_cols_X`, `R`, `XtR`, and `Qw` for Gram). They update the state in place so the next call can reuse it. When an argument isn't passed, the solver computes it itself; called with today's arguments, all four solvers give bit-identical output to the original.\n- **`enet_path`**: computes this state once per path and passes it to every call. It only does this when the path has more than one alpha.\n- **New helper `_sparse_norm2_cols`**: computes the weighted column norms of the centered sparse `X`, using the same per-nonzero formula as the solver.\n\n## Needs careful review: why dense is handled differently\nOn dense `X`, CV estimators choose `alpha_` from last-bit noise. Low-noise problems give long stretches of identical coefficient columns, and computing `X_test @ coefs` adds about 1e-16 of noise that depends on the column's position. My first version carried the residuals along the whole path, and that changed `alpha_` in about 15% of problems shaped like the script's.\n\nSo the dense solvers (single-output and dense multi-task) use the carried `R`/`XtR` only for the first convergence check. That check is what lets the many alphas needing no updates return almost for free. When updates are needed, `R` is first recomputed exactly as before, so dense coefficient paths are bit-identical to the original.\n\nThe sparse and Gram solvers keep carrying their state, with small last-bit differences that stay within tolerance:\n- **Sparse:** sparse `X_test @ coefs` adds no position-dependent noise, so ties stay exact and no flips showed up in 140 sparse CV fits.\n- **Gram:** recomputing `Q @ w` exactly would remove nearly all of the Gram speedup (0.33 s vs 0.39 s originally).\n\n**Open issue:** default `LassoCV`/`ElasticNetCV` with `precompute='auto'` on dense `X` with more samples than features uses the Gram solver. It can pick a different `alpha_` than before (4 of 30 problems shaped like the script's). That setup isn't in the required list.\n\nOne more detail: with an intercept, the sparse solver now computes `R_sum` as `sum(R)` when `R` is passed. Both that and the original's sum are rounding noise around zero.\n\n## Timings (seconds, original → new)\n\n| Workload case | Before | After |\n|---|---|---|\n| `enet_path`, dense | 0.433 | 0.168 |\n| `LassoCV`, dense | 0.247 | 0.073 |\n| `enet_path`, Gram | 0.390 | 0.079 |\n| `MultiTaskElasticNetCV`, dense | 0.316 | 0.206 |\n\nOn sparse CSC benchmarks I built (shaped 20000×400 and 10000×300×3):\n- **With an intercept:** `LassoCV` is about 11–12x faster and `MultiTaskLassoCV` about 20x.\n- **Without an intercept:** both are only about 1.4x faster. It only does this when the path has more than one alpha.\n- **New helper `_sparse_norm2_cols`**: computes the weighted column norms of the centered sparse `X`, using the same per-nonzero formula as the solver.\n\n## Needs careful review: why dense is handled differently\nOn dense `X`, CV estimators choose `alpha_` from last-bit noise. Low-noise problems give long stretches of identical coefficient columns, and computing `X_test @ coefs` adds about 1e-16 of noise that depends on the column's position. My first version carried the residuals along the whole path, and that changed `alpha_` in about 15% of problems shaped like the script's.\n\nSo the dense solvers (single-output and dense multi-task) use the carried `R`/`XtR` only for the first convergence check. That check is what lets the many alphas needing no updates return almost for free. It can pick a different `alpha_` than before (4 of 30 problems shaped like the script's). That setup isn't in the required list.\n\nOne more detail: with an intercept, the sparse solver now computes `R_sum` as `sum(R)` when `R` is passed.
